blockers.description: detect_devices.py's resolve_port_identity() has a real, confirmed bug: it treats 'connect + write_calibration() completes without an exception' as proof of robot identity. This is NOT reliable — during this session's live run, the FOLLOWER's real physical port (/dev/cu.usbmodem5B8E1139151) was checked against the FOLLOWER id first (failed on motor 5, 'no status packet'), then checked against the LEADER id ('soarm_leader_01') and that check SUCCEEDED (no exception raised) even though this is physically the follower arm, not the leader. Evidence: resolve_port_identity() only prints on failure; the transcript shows a follower-id failure on that port immediately followed by silence (no leader-id failure printed) and then the top-level 'no port resolved to follower' error — the only way that sequence happens is if the leader-id check on that port returned True. Because resolve_port_identity() calls write_calibration() (Homing_Offset, Min_Position_Limit, Max_Position_Limit) as part of its 'test', this means the LEADER's saved calibration values were likely WRITTEN onto the FOLLOWER's real servos, believing it was the leader. Follower and leader are physically different builds (30kg-cm servos vs. the leader's original 7.4V servos per this project's own hardware history) so their calibration ranges are not interchangeable.
blockers.workaround: NONE YET — do not send any further motion commands to the follower (no e-stop retest, no live episode) until its actual on-servo calibration (Homing_Offset/Min_Position_Limit/Max_Position_Limit) is read back and verified/restored against its own true calibration file, not the leader's. device_map.json was NOT written to disk (main() raises SystemExit before the write on DeviceDetectionError), so this is contained to the servos' own EEPROM, not a committed config file.

context_notes: This pause is NOT a normal 'waiting on the user' pause — it's a mid-investigation pause after finding a real, live hardware safety issue during Task 3 prep. The phase's centerpiece live episode (Task 3) is on hold until the follower's calibration is confirmed correct. The device auto-discovery script built in Task 2 (control/detect_devices.py, commit fa99468) has a design flaw: its per-port identity test (resolve_port_identity in the worktree's control/detect_devices.py) considers 'no exception during connect+write_calibration' as proof of identity, which is not actually a valid identity signal since both arms' motor IDs/ranges overlap enough that a wrong calibration file can write successfully. This needs a real fix (e.g. read something uniquely identifying — serial number, or compare read-back values against expected ranges before trusting a write cycle) before detect_devices.py is trusted again. The open worktree (.claude/worktrees/agent-afe9e290a91f86d2e, branch worktree-agent-afe9e290a91f86d2e, HEAD 6ca93fe) still holds Tasks 1-2's work, unmerged to master, same as before.
